content.title: 'Paradise' Season 2 Finale: What To Know About Blucifer The Horse And Denver Airport Bunker Conspiracies
content.text: Published March 30, 2026, 2:00 p.m. ET Where to Stream: Paradise Where to Watch Widget Failed To Load. Please Try Again. Powered by Reelgood Welp, Paradise finally went there. And by there, we mean the Denver International Airport, of course! Paradise Season 2, Episode 8 spoilers ahead. Paradise‘s Season 2 finale, “Exodus,” took viewers on a wild, explosive ride. The OG bunker blew, Sinatra (Julianne Nicholson) went down with the ship, and we finally learned what (and where) the heck Alex is! A flashback revealed that Alex is an advanced AI-controlled quantum computer built by boy genius Dylan/Link (Thomas Doherty) alongside quantum mechanics professor Henry Miller (Patrick Fischler). Sinatra funded the project in hopes of getting access to the fastest computer possible and solving the climate crisis before it became a catastrophe. While catastrophe clearly struck before Sinatra could prevent it, as she told Xavier (Sterling K. Brown) before she died, there’s still hope to stop all of the tragedy that’s occurred. All Xavier has to do is head to a second bunker 100 miles away from Paradise, locate Alex, and follow the quantum computer’s instructions. Oh, and that second bunker is located deep underneath the Denver Airport!!!! (Yes, I screamed!) If you know anything about the Denver International Airport and the slew of conspiracy theories surrounding it, you’ll understand why it’s so dramatic, hilarious, iconic, and incredibly on-the-nose that Paradise‘s most sci-fi season yet ended there. If you’re unfamiliar with the mysterious airport and its history or simply want to brush up, read on! Here’s what to know about Paradise‘s Denver Airport twist, the massive blue horse sculpture on top of Alex, the many Denver Airport conspiracy theories and bunker theories, and why it’s so crucial that Paradise was set in Colorado. Paradise‘s Second Bunker Is Under Blucifer: What To Know About The Blue Mustang Statue Outside The Denver Airport Visit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGEThe final scene of Paradise Season 2’s finale shows the camera pull back from Xavier and give viewers an aerial look at the 100-mile journey from him to the Denver airport. Before the end credits roll, Paradise focuses on the airport’s infamous blue mustang statue with glowing red eyes, nicknamed Blucifer. Then it takes us underground to reveal that Alex is housed in a bunker directly beneath it! Photo: Hulu For those who don’t know, the “devil horse” is a 32-foot high, 9,000-pound cast-fiberglas sculpture officially titled “Mustang.” The infamous statue ended up being artist Luis Jiménez’s last, as he was killed in 2006 at age 65 after a piece of the sculpture fell on him, severing an artery in his leg. His children finished the sculpture, which has fueled fears/conspiracy theories since its February 2008 unveiling. As the airport notes on its website, “Jiménez’ characteristic style references the grandeur of the Mexican muralists, the energy of the Southwest and the bright colors he experienced as a youth in his father’s sign-making company.” The menacing red eyes of “Mustang” glow as a result of LED flood lights, and were reportedly a tribute to Jiménez’s father and the neon shop that Jiménez grew up in. But some feel the statue represents the Fourth Horseman of the Apocalypse, Death. So the fact that Paradise buried Alex beneath Blucifer is incredibly on-brand. That said, the blue mustang is but one of many Denver Airport and Colorado-related conspiracy theories… Paradise Embraces Denver Airport Conspiracies, Bunker Theories And All Due to the Cheyenne Mountain Complex and real Colorado billionaire bunker rumors, Paradise fans suspected there was a deeper meaning behind the bunker’s setting since Season 1. By writing the Denver Airport into the story, Season 2’s finale validated those theories in an incredibly satisfying fashion. So what’s the significance of the airport beyond Blucifer? And why would Paradise‘s writers bury Alex underneath the Denver Airport? The Denver Airport conspiracies run deep and started before the doors even opened in 1995 as a result of construction delays and massive costs. In the past, the airport addressed the wild theories — be it in a series of incredibly self-aware ads or exhibits like “Conspiracy Theories Uncovered,” which “featured video, artwork, props and more, explaining some of the most pervasive airport conspiracy theories and the “real” explanations behind them.” Photo: Hulu Beyond Blucifer, one crucial, extremely Paradise-relevant theory is that the airport was built atop secret bunkers and tunnels for the New World Order. Some even claim there’s a tunnel that runs all the way from the airport to the North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD), located around 100 miles away, which, distance-wise, aligns with what Sinatra told Xavier in the finale. In addition to bunker whispers, there are airport conspiracies about everything from lurking lizard people and aliens to Illuminati headquarters, apocalyptic murals, swastika-shaped runways, and more. It’s even believed that there’s a time capsule buried beneath the airport’s dedication stone, which is meant to be unearthed in 2094. As New York Magazine reported, “The airport’s dedication stone features the Masonic Square and Compasses insignia and names the main funder of the project not as the City of Denver or the State of Colorado but the ‘New World Airport Commission.’ Of course, no such organization seems to exist.” Before Paradise‘s Season 2 finale concluded, Sinatra told Xavier, “100 miles from here, there’s a second bunker deep underneath the Denver Airport. It houses a quantum computer that can stop all of this. In fact, it already has stopped all of this. You just need to get there and follow its instructions.” So it’s safe to say that Paradise Season 3 will dive even deeper into the Denver Airport’s mysteries and the bunker below Blucifer. Photo: Hulu While you wait for Paradise to return, we highly suggest diving into the Denver Airport rabbit hole to learn more about the theories and ensure you’re ready for any other real-world references the writers have in store. And stay tuned for more Paradise Season 3 updates from Decider. Paradise Season 2 is now streaming on Hulu. Tags dan fogelman Hulu Paradise
